title: Shuttle: Dependency-Attributed Workflow Evolution for Smart Contract Auditing
title_zh: Shuttle：基于依赖归因的智能合约审计工作流演化
abstract_en: In LLM-based smart contract auditing, detection quality depends on both model capability and workflow design. While coding agents can revise workflows from execution feedback, unconstrained rewrites rarely yield stable gains. Cross-function vulnerabilities require multi-step state tracking and boundary reasoning that coarse pipelines miss. End-to-end outcomes hide which step lost a clue, so direct rewrites regress existing hits or discard valid edits under coarse aggregate scoring. Repeatedly iterating on a small project set also adds case-specific heuristics that bloat prompts and hurt generalization. We present Shuttle, a constrained workflow-evolution system, and LucidScan, the auditing framework it evolves. Shuttle centers on provenance-graph attribution: it expands each run into an instance-level dependency graph, locates the node where a clue was lost via forward search, and traces existing hits backward into a protected set. After evaluating a merged batch, Shuttle drops dragging edits via a node-level provenance ledger, falling back to cache-reusing local re-runs only when early-round edits overlap on the same node. For localized bottlenecks, Shuttle generates edits under task decomposition, progressive refinement, and generality blind review. On 10 training projects, Shuttle evolves LucidScan from $G_0$ (28.7% per-project average C/H/M recall) to $G_8$ (82.1%). On 13 held-out validation projects under the same model, average recall rises from 28.6% ($G_0$) to 70.3% ($G_8$), above Pashov and Codex Security. In an anonymized live public audit contest with 896 researchers (Nov. 2026), the evolved scanner tied for #1 in High-severity recall (6/8, 75.0%), ranked #2 in scored H/M clusters (34/72, 47.2%) with 92.9% validity (78/84), and finished #3 overall.
abstract_zh: 基于 LLM 的智能合约审计既取决于模型能力，也取决于工作流设计。跨函数漏洞需要多步状态追踪和边界推理，而端到端评分难以指出线索在哪一步丢失，也难以区分有效修改与导致已有检出结果退化的修改。反复在少量项目上迭代还容易引入案例特定的启发规则，使提示词膨胀并削弱泛化能力。论文提出受约束的工作流演化系统 Shuttle，并用它改进审计框架 LucidScan。Shuttle 将每次运行展开为实例级溯源依赖图，通过前向搜索定位线索丢失的节点，并从已有检出结果反向追踪，确定需要保护的节点。合并评估一批修改后，Shuttle 依据节点级溯源台账剔除拖累表现的修改；若早期修改作用于同一节点，则复用缓存进行局部重跑。针对定位出的瓶颈，Shuttle 通过任务分解、渐进细化和泛化性盲审生成修改。在 10 个训练项目上，LucidScan 从 G₀ 演化至 G₈，严重／高危／中危（C/H/M）漏洞的项目平均召回率由 28.7% 升至 82.1%；在同一模型下的 13 个留出验证项目上，召回率由 28.6% 升至 70.3%，高于 Pashov 和 Codex Security。据论文报告，演化后的 LucidScan 在一场有 896 名研究者参与的公开审计竞赛中，高危漏洞召回率并列第一，总排名第三。
key_points_zh: 将端到端的审计结果归因到具体节点：前向搜索定位线索丢失点，反向追踪识别支撑已有检出结果的节点。
用节点级溯源台账筛除拖累表现的修改，仅在早期修改作用于同一节点时复用缓存进行局部重跑。
通过任务分解、渐进细化和泛化性盲审约束局部修改，减少对训练项目特有规则的依赖。
在同一模型下，13 个留出项目的平均 C/H/M 召回率从 28.6% 提升至 70.3%，高于 Pashov 和 Codex Security。
公开审计竞赛中，高危漏洞召回率为 75.0%（6/8），并列第一；计分的高危／中危漏洞簇排名第二（34/72），报告有效率为 92.9%（78/84），总排名第三。

agent-harness-evolution.reason: 核心贡献是利用执行反馈迭代软件审计工作流：通过依赖图定位遗漏线索的节点、保护已有命中，并按节点归因筛除拖累表现的编辑。相同模型下的留出项目对比支持工作流改进的整体收益，但没有消融来区分各机制的作用，也未证明改进机制本身会演化。
